chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail who said:

A man asked Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) — and I was listening — about a man who married a woman with Mut'a and stipulated upon her that he would not seek/acknowledge her child. So she came after that with a child. So he was intense in the denial of the child and said: 'Did he deny it greatly due to that?' The man said: 'But, he was accusing her.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not befitting for you that you marry except a believing woman, or a Muslim woman, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is Saying: The adulterer shall not marry any but an adulteress or an idolatress, and the adulteress none shall marry her but an adulterer or an idolater; and that is forbidden to the believers.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on stipulating non-acknowledgment of children in Mut'a marriage according to Imam Al-Reza?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) clarifies that while paternity disputes in Mut'a are permissible, one should ideally marry a chaste believer to maintain spiritual and legal purity, citing Quran 24:3 to link marital status with moral character. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'I'timad' (trustworthiness) in temporary marriages to prevent social friction, distinguishing between legal paternity acknowledgment and moral suitability. The condition of chastity here is interpreted not as a strict prerequisite for validity but as a recommended precaution to avoid the 'Zani' (adulterer) designation if the woman is not strictly chaste in the legal sense.
